interpretationDecisions.decision: Each performed high-jump cancel costs one Drive bar with Level 1 inactive. The low Drive-Rush-check route performs two high-jump cancels and ends with aerial medium Burning Kick, not heavy Thunder. The anti-air Level 2 cancel uses up-back in its actual input history.

Chris_F narration and full input history establish 214HP+LK simultaneously. This is distinct from 6PP Tracer and neutral PP Knuckled Pursuit. Generic K in Vesper normal Focus Force is retained without inventing an isolated kick strength.

The OD Focus starter is 214KK, not the normal held 214K. The route has eight nominal Drive cost units across OD Focus, OD Seismo, two high jumps and OD aerial Burning Kick. It starts with six bars, regenerates a fraction during the sequence and spends the remainder into Burnout on the final OD move. It does not require an impossible eight-bar capacity.

Knockdown recipes/state stay in conditions, while listed follow-up commands and costs begin afterward. Every intentional whiff is written explicitly in compact/copy notation. Numeric +F is recorded advantage, not a prescribed delay count. Throw timing cues remain unquantified.

The juggle-Tracer walk/medium/throw take contains standing medium punch and no crouching-jab framekill. The two-jab dash/walk-back failure is not confused with the successful four-light dash/walk-back spacing. Standing-medium throw pressure is limited to the guarding take and explicitly loses to the separate immediate-jab test.

Two ordinary forward-jump/j.HP/guard sequences block Jamie’s recorded rising-kick reversal at three drinks. His exact strength is not identified. Cards claim only those observed landing blocks and explicitly do not certify OD-safe or universal safe jumps.

Three grounded anti-airs use Anti-air tags; three Drive Rush checks are separate responses without reaction guarantees. A midscreen side switch does not automatically become Corner carry. Only the full-resource OD Focus/Level 3 route receives Cash-out.
